post.title: How cold drinks drive Starbucks sales
post.ig:
Roughly 2 out of 3 drinks at Starbucks US company-run stores are cold (Investor Day, Jan 2026).
In fiscal Q3 2023 (April to June), cold was 75% of US beverage sales.
CEO Brian Niccol (Oct 2026): customers moving to cold usually means a bigger size, and many add cold foam.
Starbucks calls customization a $1B business, with cold foam about a third of it (Jan 2026). Drinks sold in its own stores are about 60% of total revenue; food about 20% (10-K).
Sources: Starbucks 10-K filings, earnings calls Aug 2023 and Oct 2026, Investor Day Jan 2026.
News and education, not financial advice.

post.yt_desc: Roughly two-thirds of drinks sold at Starbucks US company-operated stores are cold (Investor Day, January 2026), and cold drinks were 75% of US beverage sales in fiscal Q3 2023 (April to June). CEO Brian Niccol says customers moving to cold usually buy a bigger size and often add cold foam; Starbucks calls customization a $1 billion business, with cold foam about a third of it. Drinks sold in company-operated stores are about 60% of total revenue and food about 20% (10-K). Starbucks does not report profit by hot vs. cold.
